page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, this instance allocates dedicated CPU resources. The processor architecture includes 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for matrix multiplication, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI. This server does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and features zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance but highlights clear multi-core and memory bandwidth limitations. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall within the average range. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also demonstrate average throughput. However, multi-core scaling is weak, as evidenced by bottom-quartile scores in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read/write speeds registering in the bottom 25% of benchmarks.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with modest multi-core compute and memory bandwidth, the n4-highmem-4 is positioned for memory-bound workloads with low parallel processing requirements. It is suitable for small-scale database operations, caching layers, and lightweight text processing. It also supports basic LLM text generation for small models, though prompt processing speeds remain low. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a lower-cost entry point for applications requiring a 32 GB memory footprint without the need to pay for additional, underutilized CPU cores.
